guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Based on current conditions, the following is provided to assist in forecasting the Company's future results.
•The Company expects net restaurant unit expansion will contribute approximately 2.5% to 2026 Systemwide sales growth, in constant currencies.
•The Company expects full year 2026 Selling, general and administrative expenses of about 2.2% of Systemwide sales.
•The Company expects 2026 operating margin percent to be in the mid-to-high 40% range.

•Based on current interest and foreign currency exchange rates, the Company expects interest expense for the full year 2026 to increase between 4% and 6% driven primarily by higher average interest rates.
•The Company expects the effective income tax rate for the full year 2026 to be between 21% and 23%. Some volatility may result in a quarterly tax rate outside of the annual range.

•The Company expects 2026 capital expenditures to be about $3.7 billion, with the majority directed towards new restaurant unit expansion across the U.S. and International Operated Markets. Globally, the Company expects to open about 2,500 restaurants in 2026, with about 700 restaurants opening in the U.S. and International Operated Markets, and developmental licensees and affiliates contributing capital towards approximately 1,800 restaurant openings in their respective markets. The Company expects approximately 2,100 net restaurant additions in 2026, targeting 50,000 global units by the end of 2028.
•The Company expects to achieve a free cash flow conversion rate for 2026 in the low-to-mid 80% range.

desk.headline: Revenue up 1% to $7.16bn, below estimates; adjusted EPS $3.57 beat; US comparable sales -0.2%
results: Revenue edged up 1% to $7.16bn. Systemwide sales across all restaurants rose 4% to over $38bn.
US comparable sales slipped 0.2% as fewer guests visited, partly offset by higher spend per order. International operated markets grew 1.4%, licensed markets 4.2%.
Operating income rose 7% to $3.60bn (8% before restructuring costs), helped by gains on selling restaurants and higher franchise margins.
Adjusted EPS rose 11% to $3.57; GAAP EPS was $3.51 after $56m of restructuring charges.
Bought back $519m of shares in the quarter and raised the quarterly dividend 4% to $1.93.

guidance.summary: McDonald's gives full-year planning figures, not a sales or profit forecast: operating margin in the mid-to-high 40s%, about 2,500 openings and capital spending of about $3.7bn. On the call it said gross openings were trimmed from 2,600 and capex is at the low end of $3.7–3.9bn.

points: US sales were slightly negative in July and August but turned positive in September after new value offers.
Cheap entry-level meals for low-income guests are the missing piece; bundles are being tested in about 1,900 US restaurants, with a national launch aimed for early 2027.
Management expects food and paper cost inflation in the mid-single digits to continue into 2027, so price rises need care.
China and France remain difficult; Japan grew for a 44th straight quarter.
The finance chief said Q4 conditions should look much like Q3.
